I can repro this with a recent master by invoking `:!mupdf some.pdf&` and having the new pdf window spawn to the right of the xfce-terminal where nvim is running. It seems quite reliably reporducable:

![nv](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/604955/22152251/d9acc35c-df19-11e6-907f-1afd47c84283.png)


Looks like a buffer overflow in the `ScreenLines` array.

Using a watchpoint, I've found that `off` transitions from 0 to large numbers. Looks fishy to me.

```
Thread 1 hit Watchpoint 2: off                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                       
Old value = 0                                                                                                                                          
New value = 6795                                                                                                                                       
win_line (wp=0x41fff25c000, lnum=1, startrow=0, endrow=43, nochange=true) at /home/edd/source/vimkit/neovim/src/nvim/screen.c:2648                     
2648      col = 0;                                                                                                                                     
(gdb) list                                                                                                                                             
2643        }                                                                                                                                          
2644        area_highlighting = true;                                                                                                                  
2645      }                                                                                                                                            
2646                                                                                                                                                   
2647      off = (unsigned)(current_ScreenLine - ScreenLines);                                                                                          
2648      col = 0;                                                                                                                                     
2649      if (wp->w_p_rl) {                                                                                                                            
2650        /* Rightleft window: process the text in the normal direction, but put                                                                     
2651         * it in current_ScreenLine[] from right to left.  Start at the                                                                            
2652         * rightmost column of the window. */                                                                                                      
(gdb) p current_ScreenLine 
$1 = (schar_T *) 0x41f55819a8b ""                                                                                                                                                                                    
(gdb) p ScreenLines                                                                                                                                    
$2 = (schar_T *) 0x41f55818000 ' ' <repeats 200 times>...                                                                                              
(gdb) p 0x41f55819a8b - 0x41f55818000
$3 = 6795
```

This was not collected from the time of the crash (the watchpoint keeps getting cleared when the function exits, making it hard to ge tthe right invocation). Nevertheless this looks dodgy.

To clarify, here are steps to reproduce this crash reliably under i3 on OpenBSD with nvim in a xfce4 terminal:

 * Open a terminal on an empty desktop so it uses the whole screen space.
 * Edit a file in nvim.
 * Ask i3 to split horizontally for new windows (the default as it happens).
 * `:!mupdf  some.pdf &`.

mupdf should open to the right, and nvim (now on the left) has crashed.

Not sure if this is reproducible on Linux, or under another terminal...

> automatic rewrapping of lines when resizing.

> it no longer crashes, but fails to notice the window size changed
> the screen initially corrupts, then when you press ctrl+L, the status bar (for example)  wraps over several lines
> pressing keys makes the screen corrupt again
> to workaround it, you just have to resize the window, and it updates and is fixed
> i suppose a SIGWINCH is being lost or something

body:
Can confirm that the issue seems fixed with the neovim master. However it now, forgets to update the size quite regularly. To reproduce install xfce4-terminal 0.8.4 and open neovim and just keep resizing the window, after a short while you will see that not always the whole screen is filled with neovim. If you stop resizing it will stay in this corrupted state.

Edit: This probably has nothing to do with i3, but with either neovim or xfce4-terminal. This does not happen with regular vim.
PS. I can't seem to reproduce it with `-u NONE`. So maybe it is caused by heavy redrawing or something.
